comment: The missed mechanism was normalization depth in the low-progress Adagrad regime. B's four LayerNorm blocks preserve signal through a deeper nonlinear stack and beat D's single normalized block despite SiLU; D then beats A because A has no normalization. I over-applied K1008's rectifier-over-SiLU tendency, which is weaker than K1006's low-Delta normalization preference here. E remains best from LeakyReLU plus four LayerNorms, while C's residual LeakyReLU stack stays ahead of B.
hypothesis:
For noiseless symbolic multivariate MSE with Adagrad lr=3e-4, T=2048 (Delta approximately 0.027), rank primarily by LayerNorm count when candidates are otherwise similar; activation preference is secondary. A falsifiable rule is: among low-Delta candidates, each additional normalized hidden block has greater expected benefit than switching SiLU to ReLU/LeakyReLU, unless residual structure or optimizer differs substantially. This predicts B over D and A from LN counts 4>1>0, while E over B follows the scoped rectifier advantage and C's residual LeakyReLU advantage.

Backtest evidence from the historical matched-regression corpus: more-LN won 23/27 adaptive low-rate pairs overall and 15/18 multivariate pairs; when the more-LN model was also deeper, it won 17/18. A related five-input oscillatory replay reported the deeper/two-LN configuration at MSE 0.908 versus the shallower/one-LN configuration at 1.402. These are confounded architecture bundles, so the rule is probabilistic and scoped to short-budget, low-rate normalized MLPs.
